Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberShield Inc. Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for submitting questions via telephone will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberShield Inc.'s results for the Q2 FY2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Mark Chen, Chief Security Officer; Lisa Patel, VP of Sales; David Kim, Chief Marketing Officer; and Rachel Nguyen, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. CyberShield Inc. delivered exceptional results in the Q2, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. Our performance reflects the strength of our product portfolio, our expanding customer base, and our commitment to innovation. The adoption rate of Singularity XDR is accelerating, demonstrating its transformative impact in providing autonomous threat protection and the unparalleled value we bring to our customers.

Our strategic priorities are focused on eight key areas: accelerating the number of new customers acquired, maintaining a low churn rate with proactive mitigations, driving outsized performance in key product lines like cloud security and SASE, expanding our net dollar retention rate, delivering a strong full-year revenue and profitability outlook, improving competitive win rates, achieving robust ARR growth both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year, and providing clear next quarter billings guidance.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Alex. We achieved record revenue of $285 million in the Q2, representing a 38% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained strong at 81%, and we continued to invest in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $185 million. Net income was $42 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.72. We are increasing our full-year revenue and earnings guidance based on our strong performance to date.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we dive into our operational highlights, I'd like to focus on one of our key leading indicators: the number of new customers acquired. This metric underscores our relentless execution in a market where cybersecurity spending is accelerating amid escalating threats—ransomware incidents up 37% year-over-year per Chainalysis data, and the average cost of a breach now exceeding $4.5 million according to IBM's latest Cost of a Data Breach report.

In Q2, we added 1,247 new customers, representing a robust 28% year-over-year increase from 974 in Q2 FY2023, and a 12% sequential quarter-over-quarter growth from 1,112 in Q1 FY2024. This brings our total customer base to over 18,500 active accounts, with new logos contributing approximately $42 million in initial Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) at an average ACV—Annual Contract Value—of $33,600 per new customer, up 15% YoY due to higher module attach rates on our Singularity XDR platform.

Let me break this down by segment, as our go-to-market strategy continues to deliver stratified wins. In the enterprise segment, Fortune 2000 equivalents, we secured 89 new logos, a standout 42% YoY surge. Key wins included three Global 100 financial institutions adopting our full-stack zero-trust architecture, including our Autonomous Endpoint Protection and Cloud Workload Protection modules. This momentum is fueled by the post-MOVEit breach landscape, where supply chain vulnerabilities exposed by Clop ransomware forced C-suite reevaluations—much like the SolarWinds fallout did in 2020. Our AI-driven behavioral analytics, which reduced false positives by 65% in beta trials, proved decisive here.

In the mid-market, 500-5,000 employees, we added 512 new customers, up 31% YoY. This cohort is embracing our Managed Detection and Response (MDR) service, bundled with our SASE—Secure Access Service Edge—offering. Average deal cycles shortened to 47 days from 62 days YoY, thanks to streamlined proof-of-value demos leveraging our Purple AI teammate for real-time threat hunting.

For the SMB segment, under 500 employees, we had 646 additions, growing 22% YoY despite macro headwinds. Our channel partnerships with over 4,200 MSPs and VARs, including deepened integrations with ConnectWise and Kaseya, drove 68% of these wins. SMBs are prioritizing ransomware rollback capabilities, with our patented Storyline technology—visualizing attack timelines—resonating strongly post-BlackCat and LockBit campaigns.

Regionally, our performance reflects tailored investments amid divergent threat vectors. North America, 62% of new adds, brought in 773 customers, flat YoY but with 18% QoQ acceleration. U.S. federal wins under CMMC 2.0 compliance added 12 new agencies, while hyperscaler migrations to AWS and Azure propelled commercial growth.

EMEA, 21%, saw 262 new logos, exploding 51% YoY on DORA regulation tailwinds—the Digital Operational Resilience Act mandating ICT risk management by January 2025. Wins in UK financial services and German manufacturing highlight our CNAPP—Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform—compliance certifications.

APAC, 14%, added 174 customers, up 36% YoY, driven by PDPA enforcement in Southeast Asia and Australia's CDR—Consumer Data Right—framework. Japan and India contributed 40% of this, with sovereign cloud integrations countering state-sponsored APTs like those tracked by MITRE ATT&CK.

LATAM, 3%, had 38 adds, doubling YoY as Brazilian LGPD fines escalate—now averaging $1.2 million per violation.

Strategically, these results stem from three pillars. First, product innovation: The Q1 launch of Singularity HyperProtect, our GenAI-powered hypervisor-level runtime security, achieved 92% detection of zero-day exploits in AV-TEST benchmarks, outpacing legacy EDR like CrowdStrike Falcon in evasion scenarios. This drove a 24% attach rate for our complete XDR suite among new customers.

Second, ecosystem expansion: Co-sell agreements with Microsoft expanded to 1,200 joint pursuits, integrating natively with Defender for Endpoint, while our AWS Marketplace presence generated $18 million in new ARR bookings—15% above plan.

Third, demand generation precision: Our ABM—Account-Based Marketing—program targeted 3,200 high-velocity accounts, yielding a 22% conversion rate via personalized breach simulations mirroring real-world incidents like the Change Healthcare ransomware outage.

Looking forward, we expect Q3 new customer adds of 1,300-1,450, implying 25-32% YoY growth, supported by pipeline expansion to $2.8 billion, up 19% QoQ, and NRR holding at 118%. This positions us to capture share in a $60 billion endpoint and cloud security TAM, growing 16% CAGR per Gartner. We're not just adding customers; we're building a moat through sticky, mission-critical outcomes.

I'll now dive into our customer churn metrics, which continue to outperform industry benchmarks and reflect the sticky nature of our platform in this high-stakes cybersecurity landscape. In the SaaS-driven cybersecurity sector—where the global market is projected to grow at a 13.5% CAGR through 2028 per Gartner—churn is a critical leading indicator of product-market fit, customer success, and competitive moat. We track three key metrics: gross dollar churn, logo churn, and net revenue retention (NRR), which captures expansions, upsells, and contractions.

Starting with the headline numbers: Our Q2 gross dollar churn came in at 4.2% quarterly annualized, down 80 basis points from 5.0% in Q2 2023 and beating our internal target of under 5%. This translates to a full-year run-rate of approximately 8.5%, well below the cybersecurity SaaS industry average of 10-12% as reported by Benchmarkit and SaaS Capital. Logo churn was even stronger at 6.8%, a 15% YoY improvement, driven by our focus on net new logos in the mid-market segment.

On NRR, we're at 118% for the quarter—up from 112% a year ago—powered by a robust 28% expansion revenue contribution from cross-sells into our XDR platform and cloud-native workload protection (CWP) modules. This is particularly impressive given macroeconomic headwinds like persistent inflation and IT budget scrutiny, which have pressured peers like CrowdStrike and SentinelOne, who reported NRRs closer to 110-115% in their recent quarters.

Segment-wise: Enterprise ARR over $1M customers had gross dollar churn at a rock-bottom 2.1%, with NRR at 125%. These Fortune 1000 accounts, representing 65% of our ARR, are locked in via multi-year contracts and deep integrations with SIEM tools like Splunk and Elastic. We've seen near-zero churn from ransomware fatigue post-2023 incidents, as our AI-powered endpoint detection and response (EDR) with behavioral analytics has delivered 40% faster mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) versus legacy AV solutions.

Mid-market, ARR $100K-$1M, churn ticked up slightly to 5.5% due to seasonal renewals, but expansions offset this with 22% NRR lift from bundling our SASE with zero-trust network access (ZTNA). This segment, 25% of ARR, is our growth engine, with cohort retention improving 10% YoY thanks to our Customer Success pods.

SMB, ARR under $100K, at 9.2% churn, down from 12% last year. We're addressing self-serve attrition with automated onboarding via our API integrations with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.

Product-wise, our next-gen firewall (NGFW) and cloud security posture management (CSPM) lines saw sub-3% churn, fueled by demand spikes from Log4Shell-like vulnerabilities and the SolarWinds aftermath. Conversely, our legacy MDR service experienced 7% churn as customers migrated to our autonomous XDR platform, which reduced alert fatigue by 65% via ML-driven prioritization.

Churn drivers were consistent with industry patterns but lower in magnitude: Budget realignment accounted for 35% of churn; we countered with flexible pricing tiers, including our "pay-per-threat" model, retaining 75% of at-risk accounts. M&A activity 25%, countered by our open API ecosystem compatible with 200+ tools including Palo Alto's Prisma and Zscaler's platform, losing only 10% of M&A-impacted logos versus 25% industry-wide. Competitive shifts 20%, stemmed by our 99.9% breach prevention efficacy per MITRE ATT&CK evaluations and 30% lower TCO. Technical/UX friction 15%, addressed with agentless deployment slashing setup time from 4 weeks to 48 hours. Other 5%.

Geographically, North America—75% of ARR—drove 3.8% churn, bolstered by CISA mandates and supply chain risk management post-Colonial Pipeline. EMEA saw 6.2% due to NIS2 shifts, reversed by GDPR-ready data sovereignty and Paris data center expansion. APAC steady at 5.0%, with gains in Japan.

Our churn compression results from technical initiatives like GenAI threat hunting boosting renewals 18%; customer success overhaul with 1:50 CSM ratios and 95% health score interventions; and go-to-market discipline with 35% expansions from land-and-expand in SASE, targeting the $50B TAM per IDC. We guide Q3 gross churn to 4.0-4.5%, with NRR to 120%+.

Thank you, Alex. I'll now dive into the performance of our core product lines, with a focus on Cloud Security and SASE, which together accounted for 82% of our Q2 total revenue of $285 million, up 38% year-over-year. These segments continue to outperform the broader cybersecurity market, which Gartner pegs at around 12-15% CAGR through 2027, driven by the relentless acceleration of cloud adoption and the shift to zero-trust architectures amid escalating threats like cloud-native ransomware and supply chain compromises—think Log4j or the recent MOVEit vulnerabilities.

Cloud Security, including our CNAPP, CASB, and DSPM, delivered $148 million in revenue, 52% of total bookings and growing 52% YoY, outpacing even CrowdStrike's Falcon Cloud Security. ARR now at $612 million, up 48% YoY, with NRR at 128%, fueled by upsells into DSPM. We added 245 net new logos, including Fortune 100 multi-cloud enterprises, with ACV up 22% to $1.2 million, reflecting our AI-powered Cloud Threat Exchange (CTX) engine using behavioral analytics and GenAI for real-time workload scanning—detecting 3.2x more zero-day exploits. CTX 2.0 with eBPF agents reduced MTTD by 65%.

North America 68% of revenue, APAC surged 72% YoY to 18% via Alibaba and Tencent partnerships, EMEA 41%. We're doubling down on CNAPP convergence per Gartner's 2024 Magic Quadrant, where we debuted as a Leader.

SASE, bundling ZTNA, SWG, FWaaS, and SD-WAN, posted 68% YoY growth to $92 million, 32% of total, ARR $378 million up 62%. This crushes Zscaler's guidance, with 85% of new deals full SASE. Key wins: $15 million with European telco. NRR 135%, 40% attachment to Cloud upsells. Enhanced with ML-driven traffic steering cutting latency 50%, and post-quantum cryptography like Kyber.

EMEA led SASE growth at 45% to 25%, North America 55%, LATAM 90%, APAC 20% with Singapore PoP at 200 Tbps.

Across both, land-and-expand yields 80% expansions from 4:1 TCO savings. Investing $150 million in FY24 R&D for AI-orchestrated ops and agentless SASE for IoT/OT. Q3 Cloud bookings up 55%, SASE 72% of plan. Cloud Security and SASE propel us toward $1.2 billion ARR by year-end, multi-product deals at 65%.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we dive into our financial highlights, I'd like to spend some time on our Net Dollar Retention rate, or NDR, which continues to be a cornerstone metric underscoring the stickiness of our platform and our customers' deepening reliance on CyberShield for end-to-end cybersecurity.

NDR measures recurring revenue retained from existing base over trailing 12 months, factoring expansions, downsells, churn. In cybersecurity SaaS, peers like CrowdStrike north of 120%, Palo Alto 110-115%. Our Q2 cohort NDR at 118%, up 400 bps YoY from 114%, 10th straight quarter improvement, top quartile vs. SaaS average 105-110% per Bessemer.

Components: Gross retention 96%, minimal 3.5% annualized churn, high renewal >98% for multi-module. Net expansion 122%, $45 million expansion ARR, 60% upsells to AI Next-Gen EDR amid 35% zero-day surge per MITRE.

CyberShield Helix SASE drove 25% expansions, e.g., Fortune 100 financial expanding 40% for hybrid work. Ransomware Shield 65% adoption.

North America 120% NDR with AWS Bedrock, Azure Sentinel; EMEA 116% NIS2; APAC 112% up 800 bps PDPA, MLPS 2.0.

Validates platformization, modules per customer 4.2 from 3.1. CS teams with predictive models drive 70% upsell FY24.

Q3 NDR 118-120%, with Quantum-Resistant Encryption and GenAI security. Flows to Rule of 40 score of 52.

Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Let me provide some color on our full-year fiscal 2024 outlook, reflecting strong momentum across our platform amid hostile threats. Cybersecurity market 12-15% CAGR to 2028 per Gartner/IDC, ransomware up 93% per Chainalysis, zero-trust rise. Our AI-native Cortex protects 4,500 enterprises, 85% Fortune 100.

Full FY ending Jan 31, 2025: revenue $6.25-6.35 billion, 23-26% YoY midpoint, up from prior $6.0-6.2B. Subscription 88%, $5.5B +27% YoY, 125% NRR. Services +10%.

By segment: Network Security $2.0B +20%, NGFWs, Prisma Access post-Change Healthcare. Cloud Security $1.75B +32%, CNAPP/CWPP ACV +45%, eBPF Kubernetes. Endpoint/Identity $1.56B +22%, EDR/ITDR 50% XDR attach. Emerging $940M +35%, AI-SPM, quantum tools.

Profitability: non-GAAP op income $1.85-1.95B, 29.5-30.5% margin +250 bps. Gross 81-82%, EPS $4.85-4.95, 385M shares.

Drivers: S&M 32% revenue, R&D 18% $1.13B incl. $200M GenAI, FCF $1.7B 27% margin.

Regions: Americas $3.45B +22%, EMEA $1.56B +28% DORA/NIS2, APAC $1.25B +30% PDPA/DPDP.

Assumes no macro deterioration, 95% recurring, 4.2 year contracts, 3.2x book-to-bill $22B backlog.

Today, I want to dive deep into our competitive win rates, a key leading indicator of market share gains. Competitive win rates measure evaluated opportunities where CyberShield emerges victorious. Q2 68% overall, up 450 bps YoY from 63.5%, flat QoQ from 69%.

By workload: Cloud-native SASE/CNAPP 76% +600 bps, AI ZTA AWS/Azure, autonomous response MTTR -65% vs. Falcon. Won 12/15 vs. Zscaler. Endpoint/workload 64% +300 bps, GenAI Threat Hunter vs. Defender 22/34. Legacy firewalls 52%, countering Fortinet with NGFWaaS.

Four-quarter average 67% from 58%, competitive deals +28% ACV $1.47M.

Regions: NA 71% +200 bps AWS co-sell; EMEA 66% GDPR CASB 9/11 vs. Prisma; APAC 59% from 48% Tokyo DC, SOAR mobile threats.

Unified Platform 6.0 XDR 98% accuracy, $150M R&D ML deception grids 30% lower false positives.

72% wins rip-and-replace, Gartner platforms shift. Q3 to 70% GenAI Copilot. 92% partner bookings.

Good afternoon, everyone. As your CFO, I'm thrilled to dive into our ARR metrics, cornerstone of subscription model amid 28% ransomware surge per Verizon DBIR, zero-trust shift.

Q2 total ARR $528 million, 12.3% QoQ from $471M Q1 (accel from 10.8%), 42.7% YoY from $370M Q2 FY2024. Outpaces market 15-18% CAGR Gartner, vs. CrowdStrike mid-30s, Palo Alto high-20s.

New logos 28% YoY expansion, 47 >$1M ACV record, $15M bank EDR/XDR, $12M manufacturing OT/IoT.

Existing expansion 52%, DBNER 128% +300 bps QoQ, 118% retention, ApexQuantum quantum-resistant.

NA 62% ARR 15.1% QoQ 48% YoY AWS/SEC; EMEA 22% 18% QoQ 55% YoY NIS2 €25M telco; APAC 12% 22% QoQ 62% YoY NTT CASB.

GenAI engine MTTD -65%, 35% platform consolidation, 72% 3+ year deals 38 months, Rule 40 62.

Q3 QoQ 13-15%, FY25 40-43% YoY, $2.1B RPO +51%, 92% gross retention.

Before we open for Q&A, next quarter billings guidance Q3 FY2024 $312-328 million, 24-32% YoY midpoint, 9-15% sequential from Q2 $285M. Conservative on services seasonality, subscriptions strong.

Subscriptions $300-315M +26-34% YoY, 128% NRR, 22% ACV expansions to Aegis SecureStack CWP/SASE/QuantumShield.

QuantumShield GA, 45% faster MTTD, $45M Q4 commitments 35% attach.

New logos $85-95M 27% total +40% YoY, $12M hyperscaler SASE, sales velocity +18%, cycles 67 days 1,200 MSSPs.

Americas 62% $193-203M +25% CMMC $18M DoD; EMEA 24% $75-79M +35% NIS2; APAC 14% $44-46M +42% Essential Eight.

Threats up 62% nation-state per Mandiant, R&D 28% PQC, $150M Microsoft pipeline +15% QoQ. Billings outpace revenue 500-700bps, RPO $2.1B current $4.8B total.

$4.88M breach costs per IBM, profitable hypergrowth Rule 40 35%+.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, John. Our technology team is focused on developing cutting-edge security solutions that leverage the latest advancements in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing. Key areas of focus include advancing our GenAI threat intelligence, platform consolidation with hyper-converged XDR, and innovations like eBPF for runtime protection and post-quantum cryptography to stay ahead of evolving threats.

Mark Chen: Security remains our top priority. We are continuously monitoring the threat landscape and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure, with emphasis on data sovereignty, compliance with global regs like NIS2 and DORA, and proactive defenses against APTs and RaaS.

Lisa Patel: We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is focused on building strong relationships with our customers and partners and expanding our market share through ABM, channel partnerships with 4,200 MSPs, and hyperscaler co-sells.

David Kim: Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. We are using a variety of channels to reach our target audience, including digital marketing, public relations, and events. We are also investing in thought leadership initiatives to establish CyberShield as a trusted advisor in the cybersecurity industry, via breach simulations and regulatory tailwinds.

Rachel Nguyen: Thank you. Our product strategy focuses on delivering innovative and integrated security solutions that address the evolving needs of our customers. We are constantly gathering feedback from our customers and partners to ensure that our products meet their needs and exceed their expectations, with modules like Singularity HyperProtect and Helix SASE driving multi-product adoption.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the Q&A session: If using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. Limit your questions to one primary and one follow-up. First question comes from Becky Liang with Goldman Sachs.

Becky Liang: Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Can you talk more about how macro headwinds are impacting new customer acquisition and your pipeline visibility?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Becky. Despite some IT budget scrutiny, our new customer adds of 1,247 reflect resilient demand driven by threat urgency—ransomware up 37% YoY. Pipeline is up 19% QoQ to $2.8B, with 25-32% YoY growth guided for Q3. Our ABM and partnerships are converting well, even in SMB amid headwinds.

Operator: Next question comes from Tom Hargrove with Morgan Stanley.

Tom Hargrove: Great results. On the profitability outlook, how are you balancing R&D investments with margin expansion?

John Ramirez: Tom, thanks. We're guiding 29.5-30.5% op margins, up 250 bps, with gross margins 81-82% from cloud mix. R&D at 18% revenue funds GenAI and quantum, but leverage from S&M efficiency to 32% and channel 55% of bookings drives this. FCF 27% supports buybacks and M&A.

Operator: Next question comes from Priya Patel with JPMorgan.

Priya Patel: Solid execution. What's the roadmap for CNAPP and SASE integrations, especially with AI advancements?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Priya, our Q3 launches build on CTX 2.0 and Helix with GenAI orchestration for IoT/OT and PQC. We've seen 52% Cloud revenue growth, 68% SASE, with eBPF and ML traffic steering reducing MTTD/MTTR dramatically. Roadmap focuses on agentless convergence per Gartner SASE 2.0.

Operator: Next question comes from Mike Torres with Barclays.

Mike Torres: Thanks. International growth looks strong—any color on EMEA/APAC churn or win rates there?

Mark Chen: Mike, EMEA win rates 66%, APAC 59% up sharply, with low churn at 6.2% and 5.0% respectively, offset by expansions on NIS2/PDPA. Our Paris/Singapore expansions and localized intel are key to sustaining 55% YoY EMEA adds, 62% APAC ARR growth.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create value for our shareholders. Thank you to our employees, customers and partners.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
